hints: Sum divisors by grouping numbers according to their quotient floor(n/i).
For a block of i values with the same quotient q, the contribution is q times the sum of all integers in that block.
Use arithmetic-series sums and modular arithmetic to process blocks in about square-root steps.
analogy: Many divisor indices have the same quotient, so add them as a group instead of one at a time.
example: For n=10, indices 4 and 5 both have floor(10/i)=2, contributing 2*(4+5)=18.
algorithm: Set l=1; while l<=n, q=n/l and r=n/q. Add q*sum(l..r) modulo 1e9+7, then set l=r+1.
correctness: The blocks [l,r] partition all divisor indices, and every index in a block has quotient q; regrouping preserves the original sum exactly.
complexity: O(sqrt n) time and O(1) extra space.
